idea: A website where my gym friends log workouts and see a weekly leaderboard

result.restatement: A website where gym friends log workouts and view a weekly leaderboard.

decisions.question: How will users interact with the website in their browser?
decisions.choice: Build a simple website with HTML pages that send data to a server and show results.
decisions.why: Easy for beginners, runs in any browser, no complex build tools needed.
decisions.tradeoffs: Page reloads when navigating; less dynamic than a single-page app.

decisions.question: Where will the server code run and how will pages talk to it?
decisions.choice: Run a small server on a low-cost platform that receives browser requests and sends back data or pages.
decisions.why: Keeps workout data and leaderboard logic in one place; cheap to start.
decisions.tradeoffs: You must manage one server instead of only static files.
alternatives: Static site with external backend service

decisions.question: Where will workout logs and leaderboard data live?
decisions.choice: Store data in a relational database on the same low-cost hosting platform.
decisions.why: Structured tables fit workouts and users; simple to query for weekly totals.
decisions.tradeoffs: Need to learn basic database queries and backups.

decisions.question: How will gym friends prove who they are when logging workouts?
decisions.choice: Use email and password sign-up with passwords stored in a scrambled form.
decisions.why: Simple to understand; no dependence on outside login services.
decisions.tradeoffs: You are responsible for securing passwords and handling forgotten passwords.
alternatives: Sign in with Google or Apple

decisions.question: How will the website be put online for friends to use?
decisions.choice: Push code to a code-hosting site and connect it to a low-cost platform that deploys automatically.
decisions.why: Friends get a live link; updates go live when you push code.
decisions.tradeoffs: Requires learning a little about deployment settings and environment variables.
alternatives: Run on your own computer only
Deploy to a virtual private server

firstSteps: Create a folder for the project and initialize a code repository.
Set up one server route that returns a simple welcome page.
Create a database table for users with email and scrambled password.
Create a database table for workouts with user, exercise, and date.
Build a page where a logged-in user can submit a workout.
Build a page that shows the weekly leaderboard.
result.claudeMd:
# CLAUDE.md

## What this is
A website where gym friends log workouts and view a weekly leaderboard.

## Stack
- HTML/CSS for pages
- Node.js server
- PostgreSQL database
- Express.js framework
- bcrypt for password scrambling
- Render or Railway for hosting

## Structure
- /src - server code
- /public - HTML, CSS, and browser files
- /database - table setup files
- /routes - page and API endpoints

## How to work
- Build one small step at a time. Explain the plan before changing many files.
- Commit after every working change with a clear message.
- Ask before adding a dependency. Prefer none.
- If something fails, say so plainly. Do not hide it.

## Rules
- Keep server code separate from browser code.
- Validate all workout input before saving it.
- Hash passwords before storing them.
- Use environment variables for database credentials.
- Return clear error messages when something fails.

## Security
- Never commit secrets. Keep them in a gitignored env file and in the host's secret store.
- Validate all input. Never put user text into the page with innerHTML.
